title: Zeichnet 8. Kriegsanleihe
display_title: Zeichnet 8. Kriegsanleihe

title: Justitia (Hans Kels d. J.)
display_title: Justitia (Hans Kels d. J.)
observed_description: Golden gilded relief sculpture depicting Justitia. A Renaissance example of the female allegorical figure of justice rendered in precious materials — connecting legal symbolism to material luxury and sovereign authority.

title: Allegory with Justizia, crowned by a putto
display_title: Allegory with Justizia, crowned by a putto
observed_description: Allegorical representation of Justizia resting on clouds, being crowned by a putto (cherub), with scales visible. Justice as a celestial female figure receiving divine coronation — the theological dimension of legal allegory.

title: Allegorische Figur: Justitia (Gerechtigkeit)
display_title: Allegorische Figur: Justitia (Gerechtigkeit)
observed_description: A figura encarna a autoridade jurídica idealizada como corpo feminino virtuoso e impassível, transpondo o ofício de julgar para uma imagem emblemática atemporal; a Justiça surge domesticada e codificada como signo institucional, exemplar do regime normativo da alegoria jurídica.

title: Allégorie de la Justice (Joseph Stallaert, Brussels City Hall)
display_title: Allégorie de la Justice (Joseph Stallaert, Brussels City Hall)
observed_description: Allegorical painting of Justice in the Mayor's Cabinet of Brussels City Hall, by Joseph Stallaert. Part of a triptych with Charity and Foresight — three female allegorical virtues required of a mayor. Justice symbolized by scales and sword. A Belgian civic example connecting female virtue to political authority.

title: Palais de Justice de Bruxelles (Joseph Poelaert)
display_title: Palais de Justice de Bruxelles (Joseph Poelaert)
observed_description: The Brussels Palace of Justice — one of the largest courthouses ever built and a monument to 19th-century legal grandeur. The 'pompous staircase with sculptures attired in Roman robes' and allegorical female figures throughout. Poelaert's design made the Belgian state visible through classical feminine allegory. Central to the dissertation's Belgian case study and Huygebaert's colonial paternalism analysis.

title: 100 Francs Banque du Congo Belge — Allegory of Europe Kneeling with African Boys
display_title: 100 Francs Banque du Congo Belge — Allegory of Europe Kneeling with African Boys
observed_description: European woman kneeling, holding fabric. Two African boys — one seated, one standing holding medallion with profile of crowned European woman. Elephant tusks and exotic fruits on the ground. Paternalistic colonial imagery: the European woman 'civilizes' through textile/clothing. The medallion creates a mise en abyme: the colonized subject holds the image of the sovereign.

title: 20 Francs Belgian Congo — Allegory of Europe with Mace and African Woman with Ivory Tusk
display_title: 20 Francs Belgian Congo — Allegory of Europe with Mace and African Woman with Ivory Tusk
observed_description: Woman as allegory of Europe/Belgium holding mace placed on anvil. African woman at her side holding elephant ivory tusk. Explicit colonial visual hierarchy: white allegorical figure clothed and armed, African figure offering colonial wealth.

title: Monument aux Pionniers Belges au Congo — La Race Noire Accueillie par la Belgique
display_title: Monument aux Pionniers Belges au Congo — La Race Noire Accueillie par la Belgique
observed_description: La Belgique seated, holding torch, lifting veil for a semi-nude African woman presenting her children. The European allegory is clothed, static, authoritative; the African woman is semi-nude, subordinate. Racialized endurecimento: white woman hardened/dressed vs. Black woman exposed/submitted. Vinçotte also sculpted the equestrian statue of Leopold II.

display_title: 5 Francs — 50 ans de Belgique: La Belgique avec Constitution et Lion
observed_description: Commemorative coin for 50th anniversary of Belgian independence. Reverse: personification of Belgium leaning on lion, holding Belgian Constitution. Congress Column to left, Brussels Palace of Justice to right. Obverse: jugate busts of Leopold I and Leopold II.

title: Time and Justice Reveal the Truth
display_title: Time and Justice Reveal the Truth
observed_description: Allegorical depiction showing Time and Justice revealing Truth. Belgian example of the Justice-Truth triad where Justice is personified as a woman who, together with Time, unveils Truth — a visual argument for the transparency of law.

title: Justitia civilis (Maarten de Vos)
display_title: Justitia civilis (Maarten de Vos)
observed_description: Allegorical depiction of civil justice (Justitia civilis) by Flemish master Maarten de Vos. Distinction between civil and criminal justice personified as separate female figures — important for understanding the multiplication of legal feminine allegories.

display_title: A Providência guia Cabral
observed_description: Mito fundacional da nação brasileira sob a república recém-instaurada: o feminino encarnado e vivo personifica a legitimação providencial-nacional do 'descobrimento', operando como garantia alegórica da origem do corpo político — feminilidade de Estado em registro fundacional, ainda não endurecida.

title: Ex-libris da Biblioteca Nacional (A Mulher-Biblioteca)
display_title: Ex-libris da Biblioteca Nacional (A Mulher-Biblioteca)
observed_description: Ex-libris criado por Eliseu Visconti em 1903 para a Biblioteca Nacional do Rio de Janeiro, ainda em uso atualmente. A composição central mostra 'A Mulher-Biblioteca' de perfil: figura feminina de cabelos fartos presos em coque de íris (símbolo entre deuses e homens), folheando um livro aberto sobre balcão, com globo terrestre ao centro. A alegoria feminina da Biblioteca relaciona-se diretamente com a tradição iconográfica das virtudes e das musas.

display_title: Estátua feminina na abertura da amostra dos produtos do Rio Grande do Sul

title: Detalhe do monumento à República, Praça da República, Belém
display_title: Detalhe do monumento à República, Praça da República, Belém
observed_description: Close-up detail of female allegorical figure holding a flag, standing on a lion. Part of the Monument to the Republic in Praça da República, Belém. The female figure personifies the Brazilian Republic with classical republican iconography — flag, lion (strength), classical garb.

title: Monumento à República, Praça da República, Belém (vista geral)
display_title: Monumento à República, Praça da República, Belém (vista geral)
observed_description: Full view of Monument to the Republic with female allegorical figure atop a column in Praça da República, Belém. The towering female figure dominates the urban landscape, arms raised, embodying the Republic.

title: Jardim do Campo da Aclamação (Campo de Santana): estátuas do Outono e da Primavera
display_title: Jardim do Campo da Aclamação (Campo de Santana): estátuas do Outono e da Primavera
observed_description: Sepia photograph showing female allegorical statues representing the seasons of Autumn and Spring in Campo de Santana (formerly Campo da Aclamação), Rio de Janeiro. Female figures as seasonal allegories in a republican public space — note the location at Praça da República.

title: Alegoria da República (Décio Villares)
display_title: Alegoria da República (Décio Villares)
observed_description: Allegorical painting of the Brazilian Republic by Décio Villares, the positivist artist who designed the blue disc on Brazil's national flag. The female figure wears a Phrygian cap inscribed with 'Ordem e Progresso' — directly linking republican feminine allegory to positivist ideology. Key work for understanding how European allegorical forms were transplanted and adapted in Brazilian republican iconography.

title: Alegoria da República (Carlos Chambelland)
display_title: Alegoria da República (Carlos Chambelland)
observed_description: Allegorical painting commissioned for Brazil's centennial of independence (1922). Female figure in flowing white and green robes, arm raised, accompanied by an angel, with male figures holding manuscripts below — blending republican allegory with national celebration.

title: As Estátuas Fallando (The Statues Speaking) — Justiça
display_title: As Estátuas Fallando (The Statues Speaking) — Justiça
observed_description: Article titled 'As Estátuas Fallando' (The Statues Speaking) featuring a literary dialogue where Justice appears as an animated statue character. 'A Verdade: Que dizes, ó Justiça?' (Truth: What do you say, oh Justice?). Early Brazilian example of Justice personified as a speaking female figure in periodical press.

title: Estátua da Justiça (Luiz Rochet) — referência no Almanak Laemmert
display_title: Estátua da Justiça (Luiz Rochet) — referência no Almanak Laemmert
observed_description: Reference in the Almanak Laemmert (1929 edition) to the statue of Justice by French sculptor Luiz Rochet, inaugurated September 1872. Alongside statues of History, Poetry and Science. Documents the importation of French allegorical sculpture into Brazilian public space.

title: A Justiça (Alfredo Ceschiatti, STF Brasília)
display_title: A Justiça (Alfredo Ceschiatti, STF Brasília)
observed_description: Monumental granite sculpture of Justice (Themis) seated before the Supreme Federal Tribunal in Brasília. Eyes closed, holding a sword with both hands. Designed to complement Oscar Niemeyer's modernist architecture. The Brazilian Justiça — a seated, blindfolded, sword-bearing woman as the face of the highest court. Attacked on January 8, 2023, making it a central object in the dissertation's analysis of iconoclasm and legal literacy.

title: Eliseu Visconti — Alegoria (Biblioteca Nacional, Rio de Janeiro)
display_title: Eliseu Visconti — Alegoria (Biblioteca Nacional, Rio de Janeiro)
observed_description: Impressionist-style allegorical panel for the Presidential Room of the Biblioteca Nacional in Rio de Janeiro. Female allegorical figure in Visconti's distinctive impressionist idiom — the French-trained Brazilian artist adapting European allegorical vocabulary to national institutional decoration. A key example of transatlantic visual transfer.

title: Alegoria à República (Décio Villares — conjunto positivista)
display_title: Alegoria à República (Décio Villares — conjunto positivista)
observed_description: A alegoria opera a transposição da soberania do corpo do monarca para um corpo feminino idealizado e classicizado: a mulher-República encarna o novo fundamento jurídico-político do Estado republicano. A vitalidade sensual e o gorro da liberdade situam a obra no momento fundacional do regime, em que o corpo alegórico vivo ainda condensa o pacto de soberania antes de seu endurecimento burocrático e militar posterior.

title: A Justiça de Salomão
display_title: A Justiça de Salomão
observed_description: Painel em têmpera sobre tela (179 × 191 cm) que retrata a cena bíblica do julgamento de Salomão: o rei, sentado em trono, segura uma criança nua em uma mão e um facão na outra, enquanto a mãe verdadeira, de joelhos em atitude de súplica, e a falsa mãe, arrogante ao fundo, completam a composição. Executado para decorar a sede da Rádio Tupi de São Paulo, a obra foi emprestada ao MASP em 1947 e doada em 1959. Obra tombada sob nº 327.

display_title: "Justitia"

title: La Justice, la Vengeance et la Vérité
display_title: La Justice, la Vengeance et la Vérité
observed_description: Engraving depicting three female allegorical figures: Justice, Vengeance, and Truth. A powerful composition showing Justice as a dominant female presence, flanked by Truth and divine Vengeance — key triad in French republican allegorical vocabulary.

title: Le triomphe de la Justice et de la Vérité
display_title: Le triomphe de la Justice et de la Vérité
observed_description: Engraving showing the triumph of Justice and Truth as female allegorical figures. Complete state with full lettering. Part of Chifflart's series on juridical allegory.

title: L'envoyé de la Justice
display_title: L'envoyé de la Justice
observed_description: Engraving titled 'The Envoy of Justice' — depicting a figure sent by Justice (as a female allegorical power). Early example in the series of Justice representations by Chifflart.

title: Marianne enseignant l'alphabet à des enfants (naïades et Marianne)
display_title: Marianne enseignant l'alphabet à des enfants (naïades et Marianne)
observed_description: Engravings depicting naiads and Marianne teaching the alphabet to children. Powerful image of the Republic-as-woman as educator — embodying the republican ideal of laïcité and public instruction through a female allegorical figure.

title: La République aimable (Félicien Rops)
display_title: La République aimable (Félicien Rops)
observed_description: Satirical engraving by Belgian-French artist Félicien Rops depicting 'The Amiable Republic' — a subversive or eroticized representation of the Republic as a woman. Critical for understanding the contested gendered nature of republican allegory and its use in satirical press.

title: The French Crisis: Madame La République
display_title: The French Crisis: Madame La République
observed_description: Political cartoon from 1887 showing 'Madame La République' during the French political crisis. The Republic personified as a woman under stress — a key document of how female allegory was deployed during political instability.

title: La République nous appelle... (Steinlen)
display_title: La République nous appelle... (Steinlen)
observed_description: WWI recruitment poster: 'The Republic calls us...' — Marianne as a summoning female figure, calling citizens to arms. Steinlen's powerful composition shows the Republic-as-woman as a quasi-maternal/military figure demanding sacrifice.

title: Buste de la République (Agence Rol)
display_title: Buste de la République (Agence Rol)
observed_description: Press photograph of a bust sculpture representing the French Republic. Busts of Marianne became ubiquitous in French town halls (mairies) under the Third Republic — the multiplication of the female allegorical form across thousands of civic spaces.

title: Le hochet de la République (Jean Veber)
display_title: Le hochet de la République (Jean Veber)
observed_description: Satirical print 'The Rattle of the Republic' by Jean Veber. The Republic as a woman reduced to a toy or rattle — a critical/ironic commentary on the infantilization or trivialization of republican symbolism through its female form.

title: Illustrations de Calendrier et compost des bergiers (Danse macabre — female Justice figure)
display_title: Illustrations de Calendrier et compost des bergiers (Danse macabre — female Justice figure)
observed_description: Illustrations from the 'Calendar and Almanac of Shepherds' featuring the dance of death and allegorical figures including Justice. An early representation of Justice as a female figure within the memento mori tradition — the intersection of death, morality, and law.

title: La Liberté guidant le peuple (Eugène Delacroix)
display_title: La Liberté guidant le peuple (Eugène Delacroix)
observed_description: 'Liberty Leading the People' — the iconic image of the July Revolution of 1830. A bare-breasted female figure (Liberty/Marianne) leads armed citizens over barricades, holding the tricolour flag and a musket. The most powerful visual crystallization of the republic-as-woman — Warner's central case study, Agulhon's key image. Foundational for the entire Iconocracy project.

title: Déclaration des droits de l'homme et du citoyen
display_title: Déclaration des droits de l'homme et du citoyen
observed_description: Engraved broadside of the Declaration of the Rights of Man and Citizen (1789), designed by Le Barbier l'aîné and engraved by Laurent and Dien. The composition frames the text of the Declaration with two female allegorical figures — Liberty with Phrygian cap and Justice with scales — flanking a radiating triangle (Eye of Providence). Canonical image of Revolutionary visual rhetoric fusing law, allegory, and print.

title: Déclaration des droits de l'homme et du citoyen (variante)
display_title: Déclaration des droits de l'homme et du citoyen (variante)
observed_description: Anonymous engraved broadside variant of the Declaration of the Rights of Man and Citizen (1789). Presents the text of the Declaration within an allegorical decorative framework featuring female figures. Variant edition circulating alongside the canonical Le Barbier design, reflecting the proliferation of allegorical print culture during the Revolution.

title: Allégorie pour le frontispice du compte-rendu au Roi par M. Necker
display_title: Allégorie pour le frontispice du compte-rendu au Roi par M. Necker
observed_description: Engraved allegorical frontispiece designed for Necker's 'Compte rendu au Roi' (1781), the public financial report that became a landmark in Ancien Régime transparency. Female allegorical figures — variously interpreted as Justice, Abundance, and Truth — frame the royal accounting. An early instance of female allegory deployed in the visual rhetoric of fiscal governance.

title: Allégorie pour le frontispice du compte rendu au Roi par M. Necker (variante)
display_title: Allégorie pour le frontispice du compte rendu au Roi par M. Necker (variante)
observed_description: Second variant of the allegorical engraving designed as frontispiece for Necker's 'Compte rendu au Roi' (1781). Female allegorical figures in a variant compositional arrangement. Documents the multiple print versions in circulation around this seminal text on royal finances and public accountability.

title: Allégorie pour servir de frontispice au compte-rendu au Roi par M. Necker
display_title: Allégorie pour servir de frontispice au compte-rendu au Roi par M. Necker
observed_description: Third allegorical engraving serving as frontispiece for Necker's 'Compte rendu au Roi' (1781). This variant reinforces the corpus of female allegorical imagery mobilized around the question of royal fiscal accountability in the late Ancien Régime. The three Necker frontispieces (FR-015, FR-016, FR-017) together document the visual politics of the transparency debate.

title: [Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité — portrait allégorique d'Ernouf]
display_title: [Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité — portrait allégorique d'Ernouf]
observed_description: Revolutionary allegorical print combining the motto Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité with a portrait of Ernouf. Designed by Garneray and engraved by Quéverdo, this composite image exemplifies the visual culture of the Directory period, deploying female allegorical figures to embody Republican values alongside the honored portrait. Documents the consolidation of Marianne iconography in post-Terror Republican print culture.

title: Journée du Poilu, 25 et 26 décembre 1915, organisée par le Parlement
display_title: Journée du Poilu, 25 et 26 décembre 1915, organisée par le Parlement
observed_description: WWI charity poster by Steinlen (1915) for the 'Journée du Poilu' (Soldier's Day, December 25–26), organized by the French Parliament to raise funds for soldiers at the front. The composition depicts a French soldier in the foreground, with a female figure — embodying the Republic/Marianne — in an embrace or gesture of support behind him. One of Steinlen's key contributions to French WWI visual culture, combining social realism with Republican allegorical tradition.

title: Decretum Gratiani (manuscrito iluminado, BnF)
display_title: Decretum Gratiani (manuscrito iluminado, BnF)
observed_description: Manuscrito iluminado do Decretum Gratiani (Concordia discordantium canonum, c. 1140), coletânea de direito canônico compilada pelo monge Graciano em Bolonha, conservado na Bibliothèque nationale de France. Os manuscritos do Decretum são célebres por suas miniaturas iluminadas — especialmente capitais historiadas e frontispícios — que representam a Justitia como figura feminina com espada e balança, cenas de julgamento e disputas jurídicas. Produzido nos scriptoria bolonheses no século XIII, o exemplar da BnF integra a tradição dos manuscritos jurídicos iluminados que constituem o principal corpus medieval da iconografia da justiça. Digitalizado e disponível na plataforma Gallica.

title: La Liberté guidant le peuple
display_title: La Liberté guidant le peuple
observed_description: Pintura icônica de Delacroix representando a Liberdade como mulher com barrete frígio, seio nu, empunhando a bandeira tricolor e um mosquete, guiando o povo sobre barricadas durante a Revolução de Julho de 1830. Figura central da iconografia republicana francesa.

title: Notre-Dame des colonies
display_title: Notre-Dame des colonies
observed_description: Litografia satírica de Jean Veber representando uma Marianne como "Nossa Senhora das Colônias" — paródia da iconografia religiosa e republicana a serviço da crítica ao imperialismo colonial francês. A figura feminina é apresentada com atributos marianos e coloniais simultaneamente.

title: Bons de la Défense nationale
display_title: Bons de la Défense nationale
observed_description: Cartaz de propaganda para bônus de defesa nacional durante a Primeira Guerra Mundial. Marianne aparece como figura convocatória, associada a símbolos patrióticos e militares, incentivando a subscrição de empréstimos de guerra.

title: Emprunt national 1920 (Société générale)
display_title: Emprunt national 1920 (Société générale)
observed_description: Cartaz do Empréstimo Nacional de 1920, patrocinado pela Société Générale. Marianne aparece como símbolo de reconstrução nacional no imediato pós-guerra, associada à estabilidade financeira e à continuidade republicana.

title: Emprunt national 1920 (Banque Nationale de Paris et des Pays-Bas)
display_title: Emprunt national 1920 (Banque Nationale de Paris et des Pays-Bas)
observed_description: Cartaz do Empréstimo Nacional de 1920, patrocinado pela Banque Nationale de Paris et des Pays-Bas. Variante institucional-bancária do cartaz de empréstimo, com Marianne em registro solene e institucional.

title: Emprunt de la Libération (Rente française 1918)
display_title: Emprunt de la Libération (Rente française 1918)
observed_description: Cartaz do Empréstimo da Libertação (1918), marcando a transição guerra–paz. Marianne/Liberté é invocada simultaneamente como símbolo de vitória militar e de reconstrução, em registro entre o MILITAR e o NORMATIVO.

title: Prêtez à la France pour qu'elle grandisse dans le rayonnement de la Paix!
display_title: Prêtez à la France pour qu'elle grandisse dans le rayonnement de la Paix!
observed_description: Cartaz do Comptoir National d'Escompte de Paris (1920). "Empreste à França para que ela cresça no esplendor da Paz!" — Marianne é associada à Paz e ao crescimento nacional, num registro pós-bélico de transição para a normalidade institucional.

title: Emprunt national 1920 (Société centrale des banques de province)
display_title: Emprunt national 1920 (Société centrale des banques de province)
observed_description: Cartaz do Empréstimo Nacional de 1920, emitido pela Société centrale des banques de province. Distribuição provincial do programa de empréstimos nacionais, com Marianne como signo de unidade nacional.

title: En avant! Armée de l'Épargne, c'est pour la Patrie
display_title: En avant! Armée de l'Épargne, c'est pour la Patrie
observed_description: Cartaz de propaganda "Em frente! Exército da Poupança, é pela Pátria" (1916). Linguagem militarizada aplicada à economia de guerra — a poupança é apresentada como forma de serviço militar, com Marianne como comandante simbólica do "exército" dos poupadores.

title: Madame Anastasie (avec les ciseaux de la censure)
display_title: Madame Anastasie (avec les ciseaux de la censure)
observed_description: Capa de L'Éclipse no. 209: velha quase surda e cega agarrando tesouras enormes — personificação da censura da imprensa. Encarna o aparato repressivo do governo da Ordem Moral sob MacMahon. A "Anastasie" de Gill tornou-se a representação icônica francesa da censura.

title: La Paix — Idylle
display_title: La Paix — Idylle
observed_description: Litografia da série Actualités: paisagem devastada de ruínas após a Guerra Franco-Prussiana. O título irônico "Paz — Idílio" transforma o gênero pastoral/feminino do idílio em cena de destruição total.

title: L'Empire c'est la paix
display_title: L'Empire c'est la paix

title: Calendrier républicain (An III)
display_title: Calendrier républicain (An III)
observed_description: Republican calendar (Year III) in two engraved panels. Upper register features female allegorical figures flanking a central medallion with fasces and Phrygian cap. Left panel: Liberty and Equality with civic attributes; right panel: agricultural scene under arched pediment. Columns of calendar months below in republican nomenclature. Decorative border with diamond patterns and medallions.

title: Liberté (d'après Moitte)
display_title: Liberté (d'après Moitte)
observed_description: Seated female Liberty holding a Phrygian cap aloft on a pole in her right hand. Classical drapery, laurel crown. Seated on a stone pedestal inscribed 'LIBERTÉ'. Left arm rests on fasces bound with ribbons. Serpent crushed beneath the pedestal. Dark background emphasizing the sculptural white figure. After a design by sculptor Moitte.

title: La Liberté, soutenue par la Raison, protège l'Innocence et couronne la Vertu
display_title: La Liberté, soutenue par la Raison, protège l'Innocence et couronne la Vertu
observed_description: Multi-figure allegorical composition. Winged Liberty at left crowns Virtue (seated right, holding radiant mirror/sun). Reason at center steadies the scene. Innocence crouches at Virtue's feet. Lion at far right. Five female figures in classical drapery arranged in a sculptural relief composition. Inscription below: 'La Liberté, soutenue par la Raison, protège l'Innocence et couronne la Vertu'. After a design by Boizot.

title: Iustitia (d'après Bruegel)
display_title: Iustitia (d'après Bruegel)
observed_description: Panoramic allegorical engraving of Justice (Iustitia) from Bruegel's Seven Virtues series. Central female figure of Justice stands blindfolded with sword and scales, surrounded by scenes of juridical punishment: scaffolds, flogging, public execution, interrogation, courtroom proceedings. Latin inscription: 'SCOPVS LEGIS EST AVT VT EVQVE PVNIT EMENDET, AVT POENA EIVS CAETEROS MELIORES REDDAT AVT SVBLATIS MALIS CAETERI SECVRIORES VIVANT'.

display_title: Relief: Gerechtigkeit und Eintracht (Bremen Rathaus)

title: Allegorie der Jus Civile (Christian Wenzinger)
display_title: Allegorie der Jus Civile (Christian Wenzinger)

title: Kamin mit Justitia (Leipzig, Altes Rathaus)
display_title: Kamin mit Justitia (Leipzig, Altes Rathaus)
observed_description: Fireplace with Justitia in the Leipzig Old Town Hall (c. 1610). Justice as a decorative element on a fireplace in the main council chamber — the warming presence of legal authority in the deliberative space.

title: Gerechtigkeit (Allegory of Justice) by Lucas Cranach the Elder
display_title: Gerechtigkeit (Allegory of Justice) by Lucas Cranach the Elder
observed_description: Painting showing the personification of Justice as a half-length nude female figure against dark background, holding sword and scales. Inscribed 'GERECHTIGKAEIT'. One of the most influential Renaissance depictions — Cranach's eroticized Justice figure set a visual template that persisted for centuries. Northern Renaissance.

title: Germania
display_title: Germania
observed_description: Personificação da Alemanha como mulher guerreira (Germania), pintada por Friedrich August von Kaulbach em agosto de 1914, no início da Primeira Guerra Mundial. A figura feminina erguida aparece com coroa imperial de estilo otoniano, espada desembainhada, escudo heráldico e couraça feminina, em fundo noturno com horizonte em chamas. Kaulbach representa a Alemanha em postura defensiva e bélica, simbolizando a nação armada e pronta para o combate. A obra foi encomendada como resposta visual ao clima de mobilização nacional alemã de agosto de 1914, funcionando como propaganda patriótica de alto refinamento artístico.

title: [Virtudes cardinales: Justica] (La Patria Ilustrada)
display_title: [Virtudes cardinales: Justica] (La Patria Ilustrada)
observed_description: Litografia de José Guadalupe Posada publicada na revista mexicana La Patria Ilustrada (Cidade do México, 18 fev. 1889), integrante da série 'Virtudes cardinales' (Virtudes cardinais). A imagem representa a Justiça (Justica/Justitia) como figura feminina alegórica, retomando a iconografia greco-romana da Iustitia em contexto da imprensa ilustrada porfirista. Posada, o mais importante gravador popular mexicano, trabalhou para diversas publicações periódicas e produziu um vocabulário iconográfico de grande alcance para o imaginário político e moral mexicano. O exemplar é conservado na Yale University, Sterling Memorial Library, Latin American Collection, e digitalizado pela Library of Congress.

title: Justitia beschermt Onschuld tegen Misdaad
display_title: Justitia beschermt Onschuld tegen Misdaad
observed_description: Alegoria fundacional da justiça penal romântico-neoclássica: a lei personificada como mãe protetora, de corpo vivo e gesto dramático, que interpõe seu próprio corpo entre a vítima inocente e a violência criminosa. A função jurídica é tutelar e sacrificial — a Justiça como abrigo afetivo contra o crime —, anterior à burocratização emblemática do ícone estatal endurecido.

title: Retfærdighed (Justitia)
display_title: Retfærdighed (Justitia)
observed_description: O nicho e os escudos heráldicos enquadram a virtude como figura monumental e institucional; a alegoria feminina, contida em moldura arquitetônica e blasonada, anuncia a fixação normativa da Justiça como ornamento do poder.

title: Vrouwe Justitia (nude, with sword and scales)
display_title: Vrouwe Justitia (nude, with sword and scales)
observed_description: 16th-century engraving of Vrouwe Justitia — nude, holding sword in right hand, scales at left, appearing to trample a child underfoot. A muscular, powerful rendering of female Justice — far from the idealized classical model.

title: Justitia (bust with crown and eye pendant)
display_title: Justitia (bust with crown and eye pendant)
observed_description: Bust of a woman with a crown and a necklace bearing an eye pendant, identified in inscription as Justitia. The all-seeing eye as a Justice attribute — surveillance and omniscience as female qualities of law.

title: Allegorie op de rechtvaardigheid (Allegory of Justice, enthroned)
display_title: Allegorie op de rechtvaardigheid (Allegory of Justice, enthroned)
observed_description: Title page with enthroned Justice (Rechtvaardigheid) on a pedestal. At her feet, attributes symbolizing worldly power. The throne-composition as a visual argument for the sovereignty of law over political authority.

title: Rechtvaardigheid (Justitia)
display_title: Rechtvaardigheid (Justitia)
observed_description: Engraving depicting Justice (Justitia) as a female allegorical figure, attributed to Jacob Matham after a design by Hendrick Goltzius. Part of a series on the virtues. Justitia shown standing, holding a sword and scales, blindfolded.

title: Vrouwe Justitia voor het oordeel van Zaleucus en het oordeel van Cambyses
display_title: Vrouwe Justitia voor het oordeel van Zaleucus en het oordeel van Cambyses
observed_description: Engraving by Willem Jacobsz Delff depicting Lady Justice (Vrouwe Justitia) presiding over the Judgment of Zaleucus and the Judgment of Cambyses — two classical exempla of justice. Female allegorical figure with sword and scales flanked by historical judicial scenes.

title: Rechtvaardigheid (Justitia)
display_title: Rechtvaardigheid (Justitia)
observed_description: Engraving of Justice (Justitia) as a female allegorical figure, made by Jacob Matham after Hendrick Goltzius in 1597. Part of the series depicting the Four Cardinal Virtues. Justitia stands with sword and scales.

title: Rechtvaardigheid (Justitia) / Iustitia
display_title: Rechtvaardigheid (Justitia) / Iustitia
observed_description: Anonymous engraving of Justice (Iustitia) after the design tradition of Hendrick Goltzius and Jacob Matham. Female allegorical figure representing Justitia with the traditional attributes of sword and scales. Undated impression from the period 1585–1637.

display_title: Rechtvaardigheid (Justitia)
observed_description: Engraving of Justice (Rechtvaardigheid / Justitia) by Jacob Matham, 1593. Female allegorical figure in classical dress, holding the sword and scales — canonical attributes of Justitia in Northern European legal iconography of the late 16th century.

Justice invoked in revolutionary political context — a moment when the concept of Justice was being radically renegotiated.

title: Alegoria à História (female allegorical engraving)
display_title: Alegoria à História (female allegorical engraving)
observed_description: Historical allegorical engraving featuring female figures representing History. An early modern Portuguese example of the female allegorical tradition — History personified as a woman, part of the same visual vocabulary that produced Justice and Republic figures.

title: Alegoria à Morte (Pierre Antoine Quillard)
display_title: Alegoria à Morte (Pierre Antoine Quillard)
observed_description: Allegorical engraving representing Death, part of a series of allegorical works by the French-Portuguese artist Quillard produced in Lisbon. Demonstrates the French-Portuguese artistic exchange in allegorical visual culture during the Baroque period.

title: Alegoria ao Tempo (Pierre Antoine Quillard)
display_title: Alegoria ao Tempo (Pierre Antoine Quillard)
observed_description: Allegorical engraving representing Time, companion piece to the Alegoria à Morte. Part of Quillard's allegorical series produced in Lisbon. Time as a personified figure — part of the broader iconographic programme where abstract concepts (Justice, Time, Truth, Death) take human form.

title: A Republica precisa de ti: vota em Norton de Matos
display_title: A Republica precisa de ti: vota em Norton de Matos
observed_description: Electoral poster from the 1949 Portuguese presidential campaign featuring a female allegorical figure representing the Portuguese Republic. 'The Republic needs you: vote for Norton de Matos.' A classical female figure in robes symbolizes the Republic during a period of authoritarian governance — the allegory deployed as opposition to dictatorship.

title: 1 Escudo "Alvorada" — Primeira República Portuguesa
display_title: 1 Escudo "Alvorada" — Primeira República Portuguesa
observed_description: Figura feminina da República com barrete frígio, agitando tocha acesa, bandeira portuguesa no braço e sol nascente ao fundo. Inscrição: 5 DE OUTUBRO DE 1910. A "Alvorada" é a Marianne portuguesa: importação explícita da gramática visual republicana francesa adaptada à mitologia fundacional lusófona.

title: Série Ceres — Selo definitivo da República Portuguesa
display_title: Série Ceres — Selo definitivo da República Portuguesa

A escolha de Ceres (abundância agrícola) sobre figura marcial reflete a narrativa republicana de soberania popular enraizada no trabalho.

title: [Alegoría de la República española y la República francesa]
display_title: [Alegoría de la República española y la República francesa]
observed_description: Allegorical drawing or print depicting the Spanish Republic and the French Republic as paired female figures. Produced in the context of the proclamation of the Second Spanish Republic (April 14, 1931), evoking the fraternal bond between the two republican nations. Part of the BNE's collection of drawings, engravings, and photographs relating to the Second Republic. The Spanish Republic figure wears the Phrygian cap and holds attributes of justice and liberty, mirroring the Marianne iconotype of France.

title: Alegoría de la Primera República española (La Flaca)
display_title: Alegoría de la Primera República española (La Flaca)
observed_description: Ilustração satírica publicada na revista republicana La Flaca (Barcelona, 1869–1873), em período correspondente à Primeira República espanhola (fev. 1873 – dez. 1874). Tomás Padró i Pedret, ilustrador principal da publicação, representou a República española como figura feminina, frequentemente com barrete frígio, acompanhada de líderes políticos como Castelar, Pi y Margall, Figueras e Salmerón. La Flaca foi o principal veículo de iconografia republicana federal durante o Sexênio Democrático, e suas alegorias femininas da Espanha constituem corpus fundamental para a história da iconografia política espanhola oitocentista.

display_title: 5 Pesetas "Hispania Reclinada" — Gobierno Provisional

display_title: 1 Peseta "Hispania Sentada" — II República

display_title: La verdad ha muerto (Truth has died)

title: Gerechtigkeitsbrunnen mit Plastik der Justitia (Hans Gieng, 1543)
display_title: Gerechtigkeitsbrunnen mit Plastik der Justitia (Hans Gieng, 1543)
observed_description: The Gerechtigkeitsbrunnen (Fountain of Justice) in Bern — the first known blindfolded representation of Lady Justice (1543). Hans Gieng's statue holds sword and scales, blindfolded, standing atop vanquished figures representing worldly power (pope, sultan, emperor, magistrate). A foundational image in the history of legal iconography.

title: La Justice et la Vengeance Divine poursuivant le Crime
display_title: La Justice et la Vengeance Divine poursuivant le Crime
observed_description: A imagem encena a justiça penal como força transcendente, inevitável e sacrificial: o corpo feminino alegórico está vivo, dinâmico, encarnado em movimento dramático e violência retributiva — emblema do regime fundacional em que a punição é cosmologicamente justificada e o feminino conserva pleno pathos corporal antes de sua posterior burocratização.

title: Justitia enthroned, with sword and scales
display_title: Justitia enthroned, with sword and scales
observed_description: Interior with Justitia enthroned, holding a sword and scales; female allegorical figures looking up to her and two putti holding shields. A formal composition of Justice as sovereign female judge.

display_title: Providence and Justice (female personifications in niches)
observed_description: Providence and Justice, female personifications, whole-length, in niches, with attributes (ruler and scales, snake entwined around arm). Justice paired with Providence in architectural niches — the virtues as guardians of civic space.

title: Justitia and Prudentia (female personifications)
display_title: Justitia and Prudentia (female personifications)
observed_description: Justice and Prudence, female personifications, whole-length, in niches, with attributes (sword and tablets of the law; mirror and snake). The cardinal-virtue pairing of Justice and Prudence as women.

title: Lady Justice (F.W. Pomeroy, Old Bailey, London)
display_title: Lady Justice (F.W. Pomeroy, Old Bailey, London)
observed_description: The iconic gold statue of Lady Justice atop the Old Bailey, London's Central Criminal Court. Notably unblindfolded — holding sword and scales, with spiked crown. The courthouse brochures explain that 'her maidenly form is supposed to guarantee her impartiality.' A prime example of how the female body itself is argued to embody legal virtue.

title: Woman holding sword and scales of justice (Jurisprudentia)
display_title: Woman holding sword and scales of justice (Jurisprudentia)
observed_description: Engraving by Étienne Delaune (c. 1560) depicting a female figure holding a sword and scales — the canonical attributes of Justice — identified as Jurisprudentia. Delaune was a French goldsmith and engraver active in mid-16th century France and Germany; this work, held at the Wellcome Collection, exemplifies Renaissance allegorical personification of law and jurisprudence.

title: Women of Britain Say 'Go!'
display_title: Women of Britain Say 'Go!'
observed_description: British WWI recruitment poster by E.J. Kealey (1915), published by the Parliamentary Recruiting Committee (Poster No. 75). Shows two women and a boy at an open window watching soldiers march away. The female figures embody a gendered allegory of domestic Britain urging men to enlist — deploying the moral authority of womanhood as surrogate for national female personification. One of the most iconic British WWI images, widely reproduced and analysed in the history of gender and war propaganda.

title: Abraham Lincoln, Republican candidate for president of the United States
display_title: Abraham Lincoln, Republican candidate for president of the United States
observed_description: Cartaz eleitoral que aciona a alegoria feminina como caução de legitimidade jurídico-política: a Justiça e a Columbia/Liberty convertem-se em guardiãs heráldicas da Constituição e da União, ancorando a candidatura masculina na ordem do Estado. As mulheres alegóricas operam como suporte de soberania (Feminilidade de Estado) — corpos idealizados e dessexualizados postos a serviço da fundação constitucional, num momento de fratura seccional iminente.

title: Wake up America! Civilization calls every man, woman and child!
display_title: Wake up America! Civilization calls every man, woman and child!
observed_description: WWI recruitment poster by James Montgomery Flagg (1917) depicting Columbia — the female personification of America — sleeping, dressed in patriotic stars and stripes and wearing a Phrygian cap. The figure of Columbia, modeled on actress Mary Arthur, embodies the nation's allegorical identity. One of the most iconic American female allegorical images of the First World War, later reproduced as one of the most widely distributed WWI posters. Published for 'Wake Up, America' Day, April 19, 1917.

title: Columbia calls—Enlist now for U.S. Army
display_title: Columbia calls—Enlist now for U.S. Army
observed_description: WWI recruitment poster (1917) depicting Columbia standing on the globe atop North America, holding the American flag and a sword, calling men to enlist. Designed by Frances Adams Halsted (who also wrote the accompanying poem) and painted by Vincente Aderente. After the U.S. entered WWI on April 6, 1917, Halsted donated the design to the War Department; the New York Times planned 500,000 copies. A canonical example of Columbia as female national allegory in wartime American visual culture.

title: Triumph
display_title: Triumph
observed_description: A imagem aciona a 'Feminilidade de Estado' na conjuntura inaugural da Guerra Civil: a alegoria feminina condensa a soberania da União (República, Liberdade e Justiça) como corpo vivo e sacrificial que legitima a guerra contra a 'tirania' secessionista; o feminino é o suporte simbólico da ordem jurídico-política federal, articulando lei, nação e violência fundadora.

title: Liberty. "Liberty brings to the earth justice and peace"
display_title: Liberty. "Liberty brings to the earth justice and peace"
observed_description: A alegoria condensa a autorepresentação da União em guerra: a Liberdade armada que distribui justiça e paz funde fundação republicana e legitimidade jurídica do Estado. Corpo feminino vivo e ainda sensível serve de suporte sacrificial-fundacional para a soberania nacional, projetando a ordem constitucional como dádiva materna-justiceira sobre a terra.

title: The outbreak of the rebellion in the United States 1861
display_title: The outbreak of the rebellion in the United States 1861
observed_description: Alegoria de propaganda unionista (1865) que sacraliza a República norte-americana como corpo feminino vivo e combatente: a Justiça armada executa a Rebelião-serpente enquanto Columbia encarna a Nação inviolável. Opera a Feminilidade de Estado no registro fundacional — corpo ainda erotizado e dinâmico, ação sacrificial em curso, antes da domesticação burocrática da figura. O Contrato Sexual Visual aqui exibe a mulher-nação como garantia simbólica da soberania restaurada.

display_title: America pois'd in the balance of justice

title: Temple of Liberty

observed_description: Woodcut broadside by Jared W. Bell (1834) depicting the Temple of Liberty as an allegorical female figure — the Goddess of Liberty — enthroned or standing within a classical temple. A key example of antebellum American female allegorical imagery deploying classical architecture and female personification to represent republican values and national identity.

title: El Altar de la Patria
display_title: El Altar de la Patria
observed_description: Pintura alegórica de Juan Manuel Blanes, conhecido como 'El pintor de la Patria', na qual o Uruguai é representado como mulher erguida diante de um altar cívico. Blanes construiu para a jovem República Oriental do Uruguai o repertório visual necessário à autocompreensão nacional. O tema do altar da pátria — mulher diante de um monumento votivo com brasão e símbolos da república — dialoga com a tradição europeia da alegoria feminina nacional e com a iconografia liberal sul-americana do século XIX. A obra integra a coleção permanente do Museu Blanes em Montevidéu.
